speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (a) in the last 10 years, how many street hawking licences have been issued for streetside ice-cream vendors; (b) how many of these vendors are still active today; (c) whether the licences from the inactive vendors may be transferred to new applicants; and (d) how much longer will streetside ice-cream vendors be allowed to exist.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: I understand that street hawking licence cost about $120 a year.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Can I ask the Senior Minister of State what is the rational for this quantum because it is a considerable amount for some low-income hawkers and can the Ministry consider lowering it?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: And secondly, what is the actual eligibility criteria for these licences?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Are they only given to those who are financially needy?

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: It is not really to make life hard for these hawkers because there is enforcement needed and there are also licensing requirements and the administration that needs to be done.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: But the longer-term intent, is for them to enter a good job where there are better job prospects.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, in the meantime, this is a temporary measure to help them tide over a rough patch.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: It is something that is part of our shared heritage and something that we all remember from when we were growing up.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Having said that, it is true that ice cream at certain locations can help to liven up the place.
